problems.field: construct (and the sign reversal stated in measure_detail)
problems.form_value: construct novelty, with measure_detail: 'A higher score means a drawing closer to Earth creatures, that is, less novel, so the sign is reversed relative to novelty.'
problems.source_says: The paper defines this score only as rated similarity to humans and to other Earth animals. Table II lists it among the 'three dimensions of creativity', but the paper never says which direction is creative. After reporting all three results, it concludes that GAI enhances creativity and does not say how the similarity result bears on that. The link to novelty and the reversed sign are the form's inference, not the paper's. Final c127 (design fixation) and reconciled c043 (creative fixation) code similarity-to-a-reference scores as construct other and leave the reverse-signed novelty question to Review. As coded, the record gives the AI arm a novelty loss of d = 1.93 next to a novelty gain of d = 1.76 (S1-O3) on the same drawings, and the paper claims no such loss. Recode construct other and keep the measure_detail, or keep novelty and add an open question for Review, as c127 does.
problems.quote: Similarity to Earth Creatures: Measured using two items: Similarity to humans, Similarity to other Earth animals. Responses were recorded on a 7-point scale.
problems.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 663), Section II.C; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 664), Section III.B and Table II title; forms/c127.json open_questions; forms/c043.json S1-O2 and S2-O2

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds. Two independent coders, unrelated to the experiment, rated each participant's alien drawing for overall creativity, similarity to Earth creatures, and atypical features, and the two coders' scores were averaged. None of S1-O1 to S1-O3 is self-reported. Measure human_raters fits: the paper calls these coders independent, while it calls the AUT raters psychology experts.

AI was available while the scored drawing was made. The GAI arm drew for 10 minutes in a computer-equipped laboratory with the Kimi.AI web interface pre-opened, and the control arm drew without GAI tools. So ai_available_when_produced yes and timing immediate fit all three outcomes. No construct is diversity and no output was made after AI was removed, so question with_ai follows the codebook rule.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 construct overall_creativity fits. The coders rated each drawing from 1 (not creative at all) to 7 (highly creative), and Table II calls the score Total Creativity. The results text calls the same numbers a 'novelty score', a loose label that does not change the construct.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 construct novelty fits. Five items rate unusual features of one drawing (missing sensory organs or body parts, unusual quantities, uncommon shapes, unusual functions, special abilities), and the text reads the higher score as 'more atypical'. That is rarity of a single output. It is not a comparison across people (diversity) or a count of categories within one person's ideas (flexibility).

confirmed.statement: Apart from its construct, S1-O2 is coded right: rater-scored on the drawing, AI available, unit participant, and direction treatment_higher on the similarity score as Table II prints it. confirmed.statement: Unit participant fits the paper's analysis. Each participant drew one picture, the coders' scores were averaged into one score per drawing, and Table II prints N=(58) and N=(55) for every row, including the self-reported controls. Pooled t-tests with these person counts give t = 6.18, 10.34, and 9.31 (printed 6.20, 10.33, and 9.27), and n_units null follows codebook section 7. Caveat: the form cites reconciled c094 as its precedent, but c094 now codes its one-idea-per-person outcomes as unit output with n_units 486 (saved 8:29 PM on October 5, two minutes before c088). Final c010 and c096 and reconciled c120 still code one-output-per-person analyses on people as participant.

confirmed.statement: The measure_detail entries match Section II.C. The ICCs are 0.87, 0.63, and 0.91, and the two coders' scores were averaged. The two similarity items are on 7-point scales, yet the arm means (12.87, 10.90) exceed 7, so they appear summed, which the paper does not state. The five atypical-feature items have no stated response scale.

confirmed.statement: No eligible outcome is missing. The brick AUT came before random assignment and without AI, so it is a baseline, not a with_ai or after_ai outcome. Familiarity, enjoyment, and motivation are 7-point self-reports. The paper reports no across-people diversity measure and no unassisted task after AI use. All five PDF pages were read, and the paper refers to no supplement.

summary: Criterion 3 holds: two independent coders rated each participant's alien drawing, made with Kimi.AI open or with no AI, and the question, measure, unit, AI availability, and every reported number for S1-O1 to S1-O3 match the PDF. The coding is refuted on one point: S1-O2 (similarity to Earth creatures) is coded novelty with a reversed sign although the paper never says which direction is creative, so it should be other, as c043 and c127 code similarity-to-reference scores, or carry an open question for Review.
